The experiment is reframed to TEST the claim rather than confirm it.",
      "Deep 3D lateral groundwater flow and true aquifer recharge partitioning are not resolvable in single-column ELM without PFLOTRAN coupling."

  "n_justification": "The Naches basin spans a strong orographic and land-surface gradient from the Cascade crest (~1800+ m, wet, snow-dominated) down to the semi-arid Naches valley (~500 m). Five columns sample this precipitation/elevation/soil-texture gradient to directly test the 'uniform 500 mm/yr' hypothesis; if recharge were truly uniform, all five would converge, which we expect to falsify.",
  "columns": [

  "assumptions": [
    "Recharge is proxied by the simulated deep drainage / QRECHARGE flux at the base of the soil column; this approximates diffuse aquifer recharge but excludes focused/streambed recharge.",
    "The claim '500 mm/yr everywhere' is treated as a null hypothesis to be tested, not a target to reproduce; results are expected to show significant spatial variability.",

answerable: Estimate mean annual groundwater recharge at multiple points in the Naches River basin (WA) using simulated bottom-of-column drainage/recharge flux (QRECHARGE/QDRAI).
Quantify how recharge VARIES across the basin with soil texture, elevation, and climate, testing whether any uniform value is defensible.
Report multi-year mean and interannual variability of recharge per column.
not_answerable: We cannot 'confirm' that recharge is 'exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere' — that premise is physically implausible. Recharge is strongly spatially variable across the Naches basin's elevation, precipitation, and soil gradients, and no single-column model can validate a spatially uniform constant. The experiment is reframed to TEST the claim rather than confirm it.
Deep 3D lateral groundwater flow and true aquifer recharge partitioning are not resolvable in single-column ELM without PFLOTRAN coupling.

parsed.n_justification: The Naches basin spans a strong orographic and land-surface gradient from the Cascade crest (~1800+ m, wet, snow-dominated) down to the semi-arid Naches valley (~500 m). Five columns sample this precipitation/elevation/soil-texture gradient to directly test the 'uniform 500 mm/yr' hypothesis; if recharge were truly uniform, all five would converge, which we expect to falsify.
assumptions: Recharge is proxied by the simulated deep drainage / QRECHARGE flux at the base of the soil column; this approximates diffuse aquifer recharge but excludes focused/streambed recharge.
The claim '500 mm/yr everywhere' is treated as a null hypothesis to be tested, not a target to reproduce; results are expected to show significant spatial variability.
A 3-year spin-up preceding the 30-year analysis period is applied to equilibrate soil moisture and water-table state (discard first years from statistics).
Default hydrologically-active BATDRAI/SoilHydrology settings are used; no calibration to force any predetermined recharge value.
Elevation and precipitation lapse effects are captured only to the extent the downscaled forcing resolves them at each point.
Land cover/PFT per column is taken from the ELM surface dataset at each coordinate (forest at high elevation, shrub/grass in the valley).
